## v2 revision of formal I1–I4/M1, including I2 link addendum

This revision changes only fs-isolation.mjs, validate.py, parent-authority.py, producer-pins.json and this report in the copied24 source set. Root24/v1 snapshots/index/originals/consumed remain unchanged. No execution, import, runtime stage, native/cache/repository write, package closure or final pins. Exact v1→v2 bytes, line edits, unified diffs and fix→line maps are external source-review artifacts.

- **I1:** private control/audit/sole Reveal writes use captured openSync→Buffer writeSync complete short-write loop→required fsync→close. Zero/invalid progress fails; close errors retain the original failure too. They never call captured writeFileSync, whose Buffer branch dynamically re-enters current fs exports in the bound Node. Ordinary scratch calls and the two exact reporter calls still pass original types/data/options to the original API and preserve real return/error values. Sole Reveal keeps the original default w/0666/no-flush behavior; permission, seal, writer, token, bytes/SHA, single use and immediate pre-write alive/budget checks remain.
- **I2:** callback/sync/promises readFile inspect actual write-capable flags before internal binding can open a protected path. Options descriptors are preserved with one checked flag snapshot; numeric fds/native FileHandle reads do not open again, and ordinary read calls remain native. Node26 disposable mkdir entry points check the prefix and actual returned path; wrapper descriptors/prototype/path and real remove/dispose return/error behavior remain, but each disposer rechecks its captured actual path boundary. Default ReadStream is **not** listed as a proven bypass; its actual open goes through the existing open wrapper.
- **I2 addendum:** callback/sync/promises hardlink existingPath uses its real string/Buffer/URL semantics relative to cwd, independently from destination. Symlink target uses real fileURLToPath or exact UTF8 Buffer/string, and relative targets resolve from canonical destination parent. Original actual native arguments/type/options remain unchanged. Destination lexical/canonical checks still apply. Repo and /tmp differ in device, so the plain repo-relative example would also hit EXDEV; the confirmed static old-consumed file-URL example is within /tmp. No link/write probe was called. Public alias operations never gain access to control/out/private publishing.
- **I3:** all audit records use complete private Buffer writes. Any audit serialization/open/write/fsync/close error enters a separate failure-marker path. If even that marker cannot be saved, captured fatal exit71 prevents reporter swallowing the failure. Reporter validation, intent/completed/error audit, underlying native error and pre-operation checks are inside the marked failure path; a failed error-audit cannot skip marker/fatal. Error/stack and aggregate suberrors are retained.
- **I4:** stage exit is cached in memory before auxiliary I/O, during monitor polls, before cleanup and after signal/reap. Reporter data/events are also cached before their evidence-file saves. Revoke, quiet, actual exit, independent qualification and qualified restoration have separate finally/attempt structures. Quiesce's callback records sticky auxiliary failure without throwing across the actual quiet check. Revoke records its memory cancellation and separately retains publication/report errors. Every scope still gets cleanup attempted; genuinely unquiet/unknown qualification never grants restoration. A failed auxiliary scope-audit save does not erase already independently qualified memory scope. Full poststage guards still hard-stop. Auxiliary errors remain sticky through diagnostic outcome/return and yield overall exit1 even if physical restoration is independently verified complete. Final manifest/report errors cannot skip each signal-handler restoration or shared-lock unlock/close.
- **M1:** current output start now matches bound82129/4214388; current Reveal seal matches the bound1793100193532575159 ctime and1793053795897904105 mtime; fresh incoming ref matches4f264. Old46fc and previous v1 seal seed are retained under explicit historical fields. Current protection start points to the already bound v2 metadata schema/hash. The parent WAL order, authoritative actual fsync completion checks, one original monotonic deadline, conservative same child request anchor, actual parent vs outWriter identities, no ACK recovery condition, strict trusted prefix and partial recovery after later expiry/revocation remain unchanged.
